title: Carboxylic Acids: Structure, Resonance Stabilization, & Substituent Acidity Effects
topics: 6. Carboxylic Acid Functional Structure (-COOH) & Carboxylate Anion (R-COO⁻) Resonance Stabilization
Acidity Hierarchy (pK_a): Carboxylic Acids (4–5) > Phenols (10) > Alcohols (16)
6.1 Substituent Effects: Electron-Withdrawing (-I/-M) Increase Acidity; Electron-Donating (+I/+M) Decrease Acidity
Inductive Acidity Trend: CF₃COOH > CCl₃COOH > CHCl₂COOH > CH₂ClCOOH > FCH₂COOH > ClCH₂COOH > HCOOH > CH₃COOH
The Benzoic Acid Ortho-Effect: Steric Inhibition of Resonance (SIR) conferring Superior Acidity
quickSummary: Carboxylic acids (pK_a ~4-5) are much more acidic than phenols (pK_a ~10) because negative charge is delocalized equally over two highly electronegative oxygen atoms. -I/-M groups strongly increase acidity (CF₃COOH > CCl₃COOH > HCOOH > CH₃COOH). Due to the Ortho-Effect (Steric Inhibition of Resonance), almost all ortho-substituted benzoic acids are stronger acids than benzoic acid.
summary: Master carboxylate resonance stabilization, inductive and mesomeric acidity modulation, and the benzoic acid ortho-effect.

summaryBox.takeaway: Carboxylate delocalizes negative charge EQUALLY over TWO electronegative Oxygen atoms, making carboxylic acids ~10⁶ times more acidic than phenols.

conceptBreakdown.content: Carboxylic acids are significantly stronger acids than phenols and alcohols because deprotonation produces the carboxylate anion ($R\text{-COO}^-$), where negative charge is shared equally between two identical, highly electronegative oxygen atoms.

conceptBreakdown.title: 6.1 Substituent Effects & The Benzoic Acid Ortho-Effect
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ACIDITY MODULATION BY SUBSTITUENTS
                      
   ELECTRON-WITHDRAWING GROUPS ($-I / -M$):  Stabilize carboxylate charge ──► **INCREASE Acidity**
   ELECTRON-DONATING GROUPS ($+I / +M$):   Destabilize carboxylate charge ──► **DECREASE Acidity**

Inductive Trend: CF₃COOH > CCl₃COOH > CHCl₂COOH > CH₂ClCOOH > FCH₂COOH > ClCH₂COOH > HCOOH > CH₃COOH

                       BENZOIC ACID ORTHO-EFFECT
                       
   Almost ALL ortho-substituted benzoic acids (o-NO₂, o-Cl, o-CH₃) are STRONGER ACIDS than Benzoic Acid due to Steric Inhibition of Resonance (SIR)!

Benzoic Acidity: o-Nitrobenzoic > p-Nitrobenzoic > m-Nitrobenzoic > Benzoic Acid > p-Methylbenzoic
conceptBreakdown.content:
- **Inductive Modulation**: Electron-withdrawing groups ($-I$) stabilize carboxylate, increasing acidity; electron-donating groups ($+I$) decrease acidity.
- **Ortho-Effect**: Bulky *ortho*-substituents sterically twist the $-COOH$ group out of the aromatic plane (Steric Inhibition of Resonance / SIR), preventing ring resonance and maximizing carboxylate resonance over the two oxygens, thereby dramatically increasing acidity.
